hypothesis: Restricted to CL-bench's Procedural Task Execution and Rule System Application categories (where reusable habits are most plausible), a context-learning skill refined by Hermes on Claude Sonnet 5.5 from FIT-split failures only (40 fit tasks) raises the all-or-nothing solve rate by at least 0.10 versus the untouched base skill, a hand-written fixed-policy refinement, AND a wrong-source skill, on Claude Haiku 5.5, over a sealed 80-task assessment split the proposer never saw. Follows exp-007 (Fail, all categories); new id, new split seed, new candidate; threshold unchanged.
decision_rule: Units: assessment tasks, one run per arm. Score: primary judge all-or-nothing rubric grade (0/1). Contrasts: candidate minus untouched_base, minus fixed_policy, and minus deterministic_random; cluster = task; seeded percentile bootstrap. Pass iff excluded/units <= max_notrun AND for ALL three contrasts lower bound > 0 AND mean >= min_effect. Second judge graded independently for instrument agreement. The Exchange then decides on all 13 lanes.
